name: opening
text: When manufacturing conditions change, yesterday's model can stop being reliable. Measuring every sample is expensive. REFLEX explores a different question: when should a small local model ask for a new measurement?

name: live
text: This is real local inference on public semiconductor research data. Each prediction happens before its measurement. When a measured result surprises the model, REFLEX shortens the sampling interval. As the process stabilizes, it measures less often. The model updates locally, with no cloud calls.

name: evidence_ui
text: Here, eighty-eight measurements cover five hundred and forty-two recorded samples. We compare against the published GRAPE model at the same measurement count, and against measuring every sample.

name: method_ui
text: Our first two experiments failed. The evidence view keeps those failures and both datasets visible. The current prototype reuses GRAPE, with an event-triggered measurement schedule.

name: result_one
text: On dataset one, the exploratory schedule reduced error by twenty-three point four percent, at the same measurement budget.

name: result_two
text: Dataset two showed no clear advantage. Delayed feedback also removed the first dataset's advantage.

name: closing
text: Our next step is delay-aware adaptation, a fresh holdout, and a CMP data-validation partner.
